metaDescription: An open-source, self-hosted personal finance app with double-entry bookkeeping, multi-currency accounts and investment tracking. Still in development.
developmentSummary: Pre-release software. Features and data structures are still changing.
heroDescription: Rekenraam records accounts, transactions, budgets and investments. It runs on your own computer or server and is used through a web browser.
screenshotNote: The screenshots show the English interface with fictional data.
reportAlt: Rekenraam spending report showing categorized expenses and their share of total spending, using fictional sample data.
privacyBody: Financial records are stored in SQLite on the host you choose. Core bookkeeping needs no external account or bank connection. Optional integrations contact the providers you configure.
ledgerBody: Balanced entries, exact decimal amounts, transaction version history and statement reconciliation. Categories are backed by income and expense accounts.
investmentBody: Long and short positions, acquisition lots, dividends and reinvestment. Transfers, splits, mergers, spin-offs and return of capital. Realized and unrealized gains under several cost-basis methods.

details.title: Accounts and currencies
details.body: Account hierarchies, payees, split transactions and transfers. Keep original currencies separate or convert reports with exchange rates you can inspect and edit.

details.title: Budgets and reports
details.body: Monthly category budgets, recurring transactions reviewed before posting, projected balances, net worth, spending and cashflow reports.

details.title: Imports and exports
details.body: CSV and QIF imports, saved CSV profiles and duplicate detection. Ledger CSV, QIF and structured archive exports. An optional Trading 212 connection imports supported cash, trades and dividends.

details.title: Backup and recovery
details.body: Scheduled verified database backups and command-line restore. Exports are for analysis or migration to other tools; restoring Rekenraam requires a database backup.

transactionsAlt: Rekenraam transaction register populated with fictional transactions in a synthetic reference book.
investmentsAlt: Rekenraam investments screen with positions and acquisition details from a synthetic reference book.
investmentDetail: Cost-basis reporting includes FIFO, LIFO, average cost and person-pooled average cost. Prices and exchange rates can be entered manually or fetched from optional providers. Reports do not apply country-specific tax rules or prepare tax filings.
setupTitle: A private installation, maintained by its owner.
setupBody: The app runs as one Go binary with a SQLite database, including when packaged with Docker Compose. Open the interface in a desktop or mobile browser. There is one owner login, with optional two-factor authentication.
setupMaintenance: Self-hosting means managing updates, HTTPS, storage and recovery. Keep tested backups on separate storage. An internet-exposed installation requires HTTPS and an owner account enrolled in two-factor authentication.
statusBody: Rekenraam is a pre-release project maintained by one person, with substantial use of AI to generate code and documentation. There is no guaranteed upgrade path from every development revision; some schema changes may require a development database reset.
statusLimits: General bank sync, receipt attachments and multiple user logins are outside the current scope. Some investment events need manual entry or linking, even when the corresponding accounting operation is supported.
translationNote: The website is available in the same six languages as the app. Non-English translations follow the project glossary and still need native-language review.
retirementBody: The retirement planner is hosted separately at retirement.rekenraam.com.
footerPrivacy: This website has no analytics, tracking scripts or external fonts. The hosting provider may retain access logs.
